model.rationale: The polling average sits near +2 for Talarico across many recent surveys, and markets price him at roughly 66-67%, consistent with a small but real edge. Texas's Republican lean and the open-seat uncertainty keep this short of Likely, but Paxton's weaknesses and Talarico's fundraising advantage justify a modest Democratic edge.
model.watch: Turnout composition in a midterm with a polarizing Republican nominee could shift the race either way in the final week.
notes: Open seat: John Cornyn (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Texas's open Senate seat has become one of the closest races of 2026. With John Cornyn not on the ballot, Democrat James Talarico faces Republican Ken Paxton, whose legal controversies and high negative ratings have drawn heavy outside opposition spending. Talarico has raised dramatically more money and has even won endorsements from members of the Bush family.

Polls from mid-to-late October consistently show a narrow Talarico lead, with averages around two points, though several surveys land within the margin of error. Prediction markets give Talarico roughly a two-in-three chance. Most expert raters call the race a Tossup, with a couple leaning Democratic. The state's Republican fundamentals keep the ceiling limited, but the weight of recent evidence points to a slight Democratic edge heading into Election Day.
